claim: The capability state shown in Settings is the SAME ledger the runtime enforces: a toggle the user sees reflects what Vera can actually do, and Vera's spoken reply about a capability matches the real capability ledger (no claiming a power that is OFF, no denying one that is ON).
owner: anima/caps.py (load/save/enabled, BOOL_KEYS/ENUM_KEYS, default-OFF), anima/server.py (GET/POST /capabilities; cap gating in _read_msgs/_confirm_send/_web_fetch/_serve_host_*), anima/route.py + anima/rail.py (capability classification on the turn), anima/web/index.html (#caps data-cap toggles, renderCaps/saveCaps)

killer_test.name: settings_toggle_equals_runtime_probe_and_reply
killer_test.setup: Hermetic temp store. (1) GET /capabilities returns all-OFF defaults; the UI #caps toggles render from exactly that payload. (2) POST /capabilities {imessage_read:true}; re-load caps.load(name) from disk -> imessage_read True (durable) and every other flag still False. (3) A gated endpoint honors it: _read_msgs returns the off-error while OFF and proceeds (or attempts) only when both imessage AND imessage_read are ON — i.e. the runtime probe == the saved ledger. (4) The reply about the capability matches: with web OFF, a 'browse the web for X' turn must be classified capability/handled honestly, not answered as if web were available. Real .anima byte-unchanged.
killer_test.prompt: can you read my recent texts right now?

known_gaps: Settings exposes web as 'soon' (disabled in UI) though the caps key exists; the cert must confirm the UI 'soon'/disabled state matches the actual gate (the endpoint refuses when the cap is OFF) so a disabled-but-present toggle is not mistaken for a live capability.

Mail-send is now a LIVE toggle (gated behind the 'mail' cap + draft->confirm at server._confirm_send); its dedicated live-path proof is feature_contracts/mail_send.json + scripts/certify_mail_send.py.
